claims.text: Cold-spray metallic cladding can restore structural integrity to the damaged component.
Cold-spray repair can avoid inducing hot cracking.
Traditional fusion-welding repair is ineffective for this material because it is prone to hot cracking.
The component material is microstructurally sensitive to high-temperature exposure.
The proposed cold-spray process builds a protective layer on the damaged surface.
The proposed cold-spray process builds a load-bearing layer on the damaged surface.
The cold-sprayed cladding forms a metallurgically bonded overlay.
The cold-sprayed overlay reinforces the damaged region.
Cold spraying avoids excessive thermal input and thereby preserves the original substrate microstructure.
Cold-spray deposition occurs at lower temperatures than fusion welding.
Lower-temperature cold-spray deposition reduces hot-cracking risk by avoiding deleterious phase transformations.
Lower-temperature cold-spray deposition reduces hot-cracking risk by avoiding residual stresses.
The deposited layer restores mechanical properties.
The deposited layer provides protective surface characteristics.
Under aggressive service conditions, cold-spray repairs will exhibit fewer hot-cracking issues than fusion-welded repairs.
Under aggressive service conditions, cold-spray repairs will retain better microstructural integrity than fusion-welded repairs.
Under aggressive service conditions, cold-spray repairs will retain better mechanical performance than fusion-welded repairs.
Traditional fusion welding causes undesirable microstructural changes under high thermal exposure in the proposed material.
The repair is applicable only when the substrate is sufficiently intact to support cold-spray adhesion and processing.
The repair is applicable only within experimentally validated thermal, mechanical, and corrosive service ranges.
